name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Rick Crawford running with large cash advantage
Democrat Terri Green raised only $65k with $12k on hand
model.rationale: Crawford is an entrenched incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 23 points, and his fundraising dwarfs Green's by roughly 15-to-1. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability and markets pricing a Republican win at 98%, the race stays firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or Crawford's retirement would be the main route to any competitive race, though even then the district lean would keep Republicans favored.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Crawford seeks another term in this heavily Republican northeast Arkansas district, where the partisan lean favors Republicans by 23 points. He enters the general election with over $1 million on hand after raising more than $940,000, while Democratic nominee Terri Green has raised about $65,000 and holds under $12,000. A Libertarian candidate, Steve Parsons, is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, but prediction markets give Crawford roughly a 98% chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge makes this one of the least competitive House races on the map, with the main uncertainty being turnout rather than the outcome itself.
